approach: In run.rs, move the self.early_pr(&id, &c, &ctx.reading.title, ctx.ui) call from after admission/fingerprinting/remove_tree (~1645) to directly after `candidate.candidate_tree = Some(tree.clone())` (~1595), ahead of admission and every Athena check; update its comment. Update the early_pr doc comment in gh.rs. Extend fake-host tests to record ordering against the run's progress and add never-merged tests for an admission/check failure and a verifier rejection. Add a CHANGELOG entry recording no measured landing time.

decisions.choice: Call early_pr immediately after the candidate commit, before admit() and fingerprint()
decisions.reason: Criterion 4 asks for exactly this; the 12-minute checks are what waste the CI head start. The call needs only the commit id.

rejected.why: Departs from criterion 4 and the accepted reading.

rejected.option: Run it on a thread or inside the checks stage
rejected.why: More machinery for no gain; the call is synchronous and fails soft.

decisions.choice: Leave a failed candidate's PR open for the retry; add no close logic
decisions.reason: The retry force-updates the same branch; closing with the job is existing behavior and out of scope.

rejected.option: Close the PR on admission/check failure
rejected.why: Adds host calls and fights branch reuse by the retry.

decisions.choice: Observe ordering with the fake's probe reading verifier count and whether the 'candidate …' UI line has appeared
decisions.reason: The agent count alone is the same before and after the move; the UI line is emitted after admission and before checks, so it separates the positions.

decisions.choice: CHANGELOG states the next real landing time is to be recorded as measured, and labels the 12/16 minute figures as estimates from the request
decisions.reason: The producer cannot measure a landing; inventing one violates the evidence default.

decisions.choice: Criterion 6 is demonstrated by running the three checks, and its behavior guard is the full suite including the new ordering and never-merged tests
decisions.reason: The suite contains the tests that fail if the reorder or no-merge behavior is missing, so a green run is evidence of behavior, not only of style.

files.purpose: Move the early_pr call to right after the candidate commit/tree are recorded; update comment.
Update early_pr doc comment only; no logic change.
Extend ordering test; add admission-failure and verifier-fail never-merged tests.
Only if needed: let the fake's probe expose UI line progress.
Entry for the reorder; landing time to be recorded as measured, estimates labeled, none invented.

steps: In run.rs, cut the early_pr call and comment (~1643-1645) and paste them directly after `candidate.candidate_tree = Some(tree.clone());` (~1595); reword the comment.
Update the early_pr doc comment in gh.rs (~2300).
In run_pin_tests.rs, make UI lines observable from the fake's probe and extend the ordering test: push and open_pr before the 'candidate …' line and before any verifier.
Add the admission-refusal and verifier-fail tests asserting non-Landed, empty merge, push and open_pr present.
Run a_failing_early_step and fix changed call-sequence expectations.
Add the CHANGELOG.md entry in the existing format without an invented landing time.
Run cargo fmt --all --check, cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings, cargo test --locked.

risks.risk: Other tests assert call counts or the 'seen' value at the old position.
risks.mitigation: Update those assertions deliberately; run the whole athena-core suite.

risks.risk: Calling early_pr before remove_tree(&work) interacts with early returns.
risks.mitigation: The call uses only the commit id and branch name; run tests that exercise remove_tree.

risks.risk: A refused candidate is now pushed to a remote branch.
risks.mitigation: Note in the CHANGELOG and open questions; the PR is left for the retry.

demonstrations.method: Extended fake-host test early_pr_pushes_the_candidate_and_opens_the_pull_request_before_verification_and_never_merges; probe records verifier count and whether the 'candidate …' line has appeared at each call.
demonstrations.observes: push then open_pr recorded with 0 verifier agents run and before the 'candidate …' line; pushed commit exists and is not the landed one; call kinds are exactly push, open_pr.
demonstrations.fails_without: With the call at its old position, the calls are recorded after the 'candidate …' line and the before-admission assertion fails.

demonstrations.method: Two new fake-host tests: (a) admission refuses the candidate so the job fails before the checks; (b) verifier returns fail via athena_with.
demonstrations.observes: Outcome is not Landed, fake.of('merge') is empty, push and open_pr each occurred once, no close call added; PR left for the retry.
demonstrations.fails_without: If a failure path merged, or the early step were skipped on failure, the merge-empty or push-present assertion fails.

demonstrations.method: Run the existing a_failing_early_step test with call-sequence expectations re-checked after the move.
demonstrations.observes: Bad-push and bad-open runs have the same state and reason as the good run, exactly one 'could not open the pull request early' warning, and no merge.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the move changed the outcome or the warning count, the state, reason or warning-count assertions fail.

demonstrations.observes: In run.rs the early_pr call follows candidate.candidate_tree = Some(...) and precedes admit(...), with the updated comment; gh.rs shows at most a doc-comment change.
New entry describes the reorder, says the next real landing time is to be recorded as measured, labels 12 and 16 minute figures as estimates, contains no invented measured time.

demonstrations.method: Run the three checks separately; the test run includes the new ordering and never-merged tests, so it is a behavior check, not only a build check.
demonstrations.observes: All athena-core tests pass, including the new ordering and never-merged tests; cargo fmt --all --check and cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings are also clean.
demonstrations.fails_without: Reverting the reorder makes the early_pr ordering test fail, so cargo test --locked fails; a merge on a failed candidate fails the never-merged tests.

open_questions: The study test capability has no checks, so no check-start event exists; the 'candidate …' line is used as the boundary. A cheap check spec may be added if possible.
A candidate refused at admission is now pushed to the remote branch; the brief asks for this, but the maintainer may prefer admission first.
Which existing path closes a failed job's PR was not traced; the test asserts only no merge and no new close call.
